method.comparison: same job and host; matching workload/size cases alternate candidate order per iteration; retain raw samples, median and nearest-rank p95
method.interval: Intervals vary by workload; see comparison README. History runs use separate fresh processes, five samples without warmup, and report edit loop and save separately.
method.tailPercentileLimitation: With five samples nearest-rank p95 is the maximum, a descriptive order statistic and not a reliable tail estimate.

content.distribution: text edit and reload cases use one text/plain InlineContent; opaque replacement and atomic multi-payload cases add one application/example InlineContent; unrelated-content cases vary the count as recorded per row

history.operation: one new attributed text insertion with a unique actor/effect pair
history.memory: process-lifetime maximum RSS, includes fixture setup and encoding

ranges.operation: landed retained Range fixture; separate construction, one lazy resolve, and edit with holders present

browser: existing Chromium suite plus synthetic keyboard-to-DOM-check and nested synchronous applyChange intervals; no paint or asynchronous product feedback claim
clipboard: carrier-neutral private text parser boundaries and malformed input with a constant-time retained-source stub; fixture guard values only
snapshotComparison: same-host snapshot versus targeted ordinary-edit variants; eight samples of ten insert/delete operations after ten warmup edits, separate loading and first edit, plus merge/restore/replacement and following edit; fixture dimensions and raw samples in snapshot-comparison.json

loro.purpose: reference-only native cursor and movable-tree comparison
loro.install: external isolated package, not a production dependency

browserWorkloads: two Blocks, three InlineContents, short emoji-containing target; insertion, deletion, selection, Markdown, Unicode and line-feed probes with pure local-dense decoder opt-in; keyboard driver or direct ProseMirror transactions, not physical paint or independent feedback; two warmups and five samples per case and candidate
